title: replaceDispatcher() carries stale per-index price to a new dispatcher whose primeToken may have different decimals (price re-denomination)
rootCauseClass: config carry-over across dispatcher swap with different prime token (price-denomination mismatch)
fingerprintBasis: src/V2/NFTMinterV2.sol:replaceDispatcher:config carry-over across dispatcher swap with different prime token (price-denomination mismatch)
channel: main (Low footgun); may alternatively fold under the C-01 qa bundle (human review)
ledgerAdjacency: C-01 (DISTINCT aspect — C-01 tracks general re-pointing of token/metadata under existing holders; it does NOT cover the price re-denomination sub-issue). Distinct fingerprint from C-01 (d1c5aa86…).
description: replaceDispatcher() (lines 227-247) is onlyOwner and swaps the dispatcher bound to an index. configs[index].price is a raw number whose denomination is defined by whichever dispatcher's primeToken is currently bound, but it persists unchanged across the swap. Swapping a dispatcher whose primeToken has different decimals silently re-denominates the carried-over price until a corrective setPrice is issued.
impact: Mis-scaled mint charge during the window between replaceDispatcher and a corrective setPrice. Lower-decimals new token: a stored 18-dp price is astronomically large in the new token's units -> _executeMint safeTransferFrom reverts -> minting for that index is bricked until setPrice (availability impact). Higher-decimals new token: a stored 6-dp price is dust in 18-dp units -> near-free mints, under-backing the dispatcher until the owner calls setPrice. Non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3 in-scope): the name replaceDispatcher implies a like-for-like swap and gives no hint that price persists in NFTMinterV2 while its denomination is owned by the bound dispatcher's primeToken.
attackPath: Not attacker-initiated: replaceDispatcher is onlyOwner. The owner performs what looks like a like-for-like dispatcher swap.
The new dispatcher's primeToken has different decimals than the old one; configs[index].price persists unchanged across the swap.
_executeMint transfers `price` units of the NEW primeToken (IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, dispatcher, price)). The number is now denominated wrong.

Lower-decimals new token: stored 18-dp price is gigantic in 6-dp units -> safeTransferFrom reverts -> minting bricked until setPrice (availability); OR higher-decimals new token: stored 6-dp price is dust in 18-dp units -> near-free mints, under-backing the dispatcher, until the owner calls setPrice.
recommendation: Re-set price atomically within replaceDispatcher (require a fresh price argument and write it in the same call), or restrict swaps to dispatchers whose primeToken has the same decimals as the outgoing one. Document that price denomination is owned by the bound dispatcher.
